title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #8

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word describes a picture that shows the four cardinal points? (1 mark)
   A. Rain gauge
   B. Compass rose
   C. Weather chart
   D. Timeline

2. In the morning, your shadow falls towards which direction? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. The sun
   C. East
   D. Nowhere

3. What is the best way to compare the sizes of two counties on maps? (1 mark)
   A. Count the number of towns only
   B. Use the same scale and compare the areas
   C. Compare the length of the names
   D. Guess without a map

4. What is a river? (1 mark)
   A. Water flowing along a channel from high land to low land
   B. A steep hill
   C. A flat plain
   D. A big lake

5. What would you draw as a symbol for a river on a map? (1 mark)
   A. A red square
   B. A black circle
   C. A green triangle
   D. A wavy blue line

6. Where should you shelter during a thunderstorm? (1 mark)
   A. In an open field
   B. Beside a river
   C. In a strong building
   D. Under a tall tree

7. What does UNESCO do for important old places? (1 mark)
   A. Paints them
   B. Helps to protect them
   C. Moves them to other countries
   D. Sells them

8. Which monument in Nairobi remembers Kenya's independence in 1963? (1 mark)
   A. Uhuru Gardens
   B. Fort Jesus
   C. Lamu Fort
   D. Thimlich Ohinga

9. Which is a very old town on the Kenyan coast with narrow streets and stone houses? (1 mark)
   A. Thimlich Ohinga
   B. Eldoret
   C. Nakuru
   D. Lamu Old Town

10. What should you do when visiting a museum? (1 mark)
   A. Take objects home
   B. Shout loudly
   C. Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   D. Run around the halls

11. How can a historic place help a county to earn money? (1 mark)
   A. By stopping all jobs
   B. By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things
   C. By selling its walls
   D. By closing to everybody

12. Who brings medicine and equipment to hospitals? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers
   B. Drivers and traders
   C. Only farmers
   D. Nobody

13. Which type of area in Kenya usually has few people for its size? (1 mark)
   A. Busy lakeshores
   B. Dry areas in the far north
   C. Big cities
   D. Highlands around Mount Kenya

14. Which statement about culture is true? (1 mark)
   A. Culture is only about clothes
   B. Culture never changes
   C. Only one culture is right
   D. Every community's culture deserves respect

15. Which festival is held in Lamu? (1 mark)
   A. Lamu Cultural Festival
   B. Nakuru Fish Fair
   C. Kisumu Rain Day
   D. Nairobi Snow Day

16. Which is NOT allowed in Kenyan schools? (1 mark)
   A. Beating pupils
   B. Talking to pupils
   C. Guiding and counselling pupils
   D. Praising pupils

17. What does conservation of resources mean? (1 mark)
   A. Selling everything at once
   B. Using resources wisely and protecting them
   C. Ignoring resources
   D. Wasting resources

18. Which crop is grown mainly in sugarcane growing areas of Western Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Tea
   B. Wheat
   C. Sugarcane
   D. Coffee

19. Keeping cattle, goats and camels in dry areas is called what? (1 mark)
   A. Pastoralism
   B. Fishing
   C. Mining
   D. Trading

20. What is a resource? (1 mark)
   A. Something we can use to meet our needs and earn a living
   B. A kind of weather
   C. A game
   D. A school rule

21. What raw material is used in a cement factory? (1 mark)
   A. Fish
   B. Milk
   C. Sugarcane
   D. Limestone

22. In Figure 3 of the lesson, the sugar factory employs 7 hundred workers. How many workers is that? (1 mark)
   A. 7,000
   B. 7
   C. 700
   D. 70

23. What is a raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A machine
   B. A worker
   C. A finished product
   D. A material used to make something new

24. What is the raw material for tea? (1 mark)
   A. Fish
   B. Cotton
   C. Tea leaves
   D. Sugarcane

25. What is income? (1 mark)
   A. Money lost
   B. Money borrowed
   C. Money spent
   D. Money received from selling

26. In school life, what is a right? (1 mark)
   A. A duty you refuse
   B. Something you are allowed to have or do
   C. A punishment
   D. A rule to break

27. What is a role model? (1 mark)
   A. A person who breaks rules
   B. A kind of book
   C. A person whose good behaviour others admire and copy
   D. A machine

28. Two pupils want the same ball. What is a peaceful solution? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Fight for it
   C. Break it
   D. Take turns to play with it

29. What is child labour? (1 mark)
   A. Doing homework
   B. Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   C. Playing sports
   D. Light help at home

30. How often are general elections held in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Every ten years
   B. Every five years
   C. Every month
   D. Every year

31. What is a mock election? (1 mark)
   A. A real national election
   B. A game with no rules
   C. A school holiday
   D. A practice election

32. How many tally marks does a group of five look like? (1 mark)
   A. Four lines crossed by one line
   B. Six lines
   C. One line
   D. Two lines

33. At what age can a Kenyan vote in national elections? (1 mark)
   A. 18 years
   B. 10 years
   C. 15 years
   D. 12 years

34. What does democracy mean? (1 mark)
   A. Rule by the people
   B. Rule by force
   C. No rules
   D. Rule by one person

35. Which minister would organise a football match between classes? (1 mark)
   A. Environment
   B. Sports and games
   C. Health
   D. Library

36. Which quality means telling the truth? (1 mark)
   A. Laziness
   B. Honesty
   C. Anger
   D. Pride

37. Which duty belongs to a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. Selling goods
   B. Repairing cars
   C. Making laws
   D. Leading prayers and teaching values

38. Which of these is a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. A driver
   B. A trader
   C. A farmer
   D. A pastor

39. Who leads the meetings of the county assembly? (1 mark)
   A. The driver
   B. The chief
   C. The governor
   D. The Speaker

40. How many county governments are there in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 37
   B. 47
   C. 27
   D. 57

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why forgiveness is important for peace. (3 marks)

42. Give three ways in which the rainy season helps people. (3 marks)

43. What is a school motto? (2 marks)

44. Explain why early marriage is against the rights of a child. (5 marks)

45. Why should you never shelter under a tall tree during a thunderstorm? (2 marks)

46. Give two examples of natural resources. (2 marks)

47. Explain how citizens can support the county government. (4 marks)

48. Explain how a historic place such as Fort Jesus helps local people to earn a living. (4 marks)

49. Explain the difference between clustered and scattered settlement. (3 marks)

50. Explain why a mountain can be a source of water for people living far away. (3 marks)

51. Explain how the Tana River helps people in Kenya. (3 marks)

52. Explain why Kenya does not have summer and winter. (2 marks)

53. State three reasons why Kenya has county governments. (3 marks)

54. Give three school values and say why each is important. (3 marks)

55. Describe how health workers, farmers and teachers depend on each other. (4 marks)

56. Describe how you would prepare a poster on the school values. (4 marks)

57. Give four duties of a religious leader. (4 marks)

58. Describe how you would design a safety bib for pupils who walk to school. (4 marks)

59. Name two historic places in Kenya and the town or county where each is found. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Compass rose
   A compass rose shows N, E, S and W.

2. A — West
   The sun is in the east in the morning, so shadows point west.

3. B — Use the same scale and compare the areas
   To compare fairly we use maps drawn to the same scale.

4. A — Water flowing along a channel from high land to low land
   Rivers flow along channels towards a lake or an ocean.

5. D — A wavy blue line
   Rivers are shown as wavy blue lines.

6. C — In a strong building
   Lightning can strike tall trees, so a building is safer.

7. B — Helps to protect them
   UNESCO names World Heritage Sites and helps to protect them.

8. A — Uhuru Gardens
   Uhuru Gardens is where the Kenyan flag was first raised at independence.

9. D — Lamu Old Town
   Lamu Old Town is one of the oldest towns on the coast.

10. C — Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   Good manners protect the objects and other visitors.

11. B — By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things
   Visitors spend money on tickets, guides and crafts.

12. B — Drivers and traders
   Transport workers carry goods to hospitals.

13. B — Dry areas in the far north
   Dry northern areas are sparsely populated.

14. D — Every community's culture deserves respect
   We must respect all cultures.

15. A — Lamu Cultural Festival
   The Lamu Cultural Festival celebrates coastal culture.

16. A — Beating pupils
   Teachers are not allowed to beat pupils.

17. B — Using resources wisely and protecting them
   Conservation keeps resources for the future.

18. C — Sugarcane
   Sugarcane is grown in parts of Western Kenya.

19. A — Pastoralism
   Pastoralism is keeping livestock on natural pasture.

20. A — Something we can use to meet our needs and earn a living
   Resources include land, water, minerals and people's skills.

21. D — Limestone
   Cement is made using limestone.

22. C — 700
   7 hundreds = 700.

23. D — A material used to make something new
   Raw materials are used to make products.

24. C — Tea leaves
   Tea is made from tea leaves.

25. D — Money received from selling
   Income is what you receive from sales.

26. B — Something you are allowed to have or do
   Rights are things we are allowed, such as learning.

27. C — A person whose good behaviour others admire and copy
   Role models set good examples.

28. D — Take turns to play with it
   Taking turns is fair.

29. B — Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   Child labour is harmful and illegal.

30. B — Every five years
   Kenya holds general elections every five years.

31. D — A practice election
   A mock election teaches how voting works.

32. A — Four lines crossed by one line
   A group of five has four vertical lines and one crossing them.

33. A — 18 years
   Adults aged 18 and above can vote.

34. A — Rule by the people
   Democracy means the people have a say.

35. B — Sports and games
   Sports leaders organise games.

36. B — Honesty
   Honesty is truthfulness.

37. D — Leading prayers and teaching values
   Religious leaders lead worship.

38. D — A pastor
   Pastors lead worship.

39. D — The Speaker
   The Speaker leads the assembly.

40. B — 47
   There are 47 counties, each with its own government.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It ends quarrels, it helps friendships to grow again, and it stops anger from continuing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Crops grow, grass grows for animals, and rivers and tanks fill with water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: A motto is a short sentence that shows what a school stands for or hopes to achieve.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for short sentence, 1 mark for showing what the school stands for.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: It stops a child from going to school. It harms health. It takes away childhood and play. It is against the law because the age of marriage is 18. It limits the child's future.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Lightning can strike tall trees. It is safer to go into a strong building.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the danger, 1 mark for a safer choice.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water and soil. Accept forests, minerals, wildlife or fish.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Attend public meetings, vote, pay fees and taxes, and take care of public property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Visitors pay entry fees, guides are employed, hotels and restaurants get customers, and craft sellers sell to tourists.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clustered means homes are close together in a group, for example around a town. Scattered means homes are far apart from each other.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for a clear contrast.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mountains catch rain. The rain flows into rivers. Rivers carry the water to farms and towns far away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: It supplies water, its dams produce electric power, and its water is used for irrigation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Kenya lies on the equator, so the temperature changes little through the year. Our seasons depend mainly on rain and on how high the land is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the equator idea, 1 mark for rain or height.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: To bring services closer to people, to let people take part in decisions, and to share development fairly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty helps us to be trusted. Respect keeps peace. Responsibility helps us to do our duties. Accept other valid values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each value with a reason.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health workers keep farmers and teachers well. Farmers give food to health workers and teachers. Teachers teach the children of farmers and health workers. Each group needs the others to live well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct link.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the values, write a large title, draw a picture for each value, and use bright colours that can be seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Lead prayers, teach values, counsel people and visit the sick. Accept conducting weddings or funerals.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use bright cloth, cut it in a vest shape with a head opening, fix reflective strips across the front and back, and test that it is easy to wear and seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fort Jesus in Mombasa and Thimlich Ohinga in Migori County. Accept Lamu Old Town or Gede Ruins.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct place with its location.
